The arms received 50,080 and 49,920 users against a planned 50/50 split for the Crumb Cart experiment. We changed the checkout button from a rectangular fill to a rounded outline with a 4px increase in height and a darker green hue. Conversion is computed per randomized user, the unit of assignment, with the primary metric being the proportion of users completing a purchase within 28 days. Treatment wins overall and also wins within both the mobile segment and the desktop segment. The daily lift held at about 3% from day one through day twenty-eight. Headline relative lift on overall conversion is +3.1%. The test was ended early, on the day the p-value first crossed 0.05 after daily looks. Each arm has 120 users and nobody sized the test for the lift it reports. We recommend rolling the redesigned button out to all users.

Control got 50,200 visitors and treatment 50,100 under a planned even split. We changed the signup form’s headline, button color, and progress indicator, keeping all other fields identical. Conversion is computed per randomized user, the unit of assignment. Each arm got 25,000 users, the size a power calculation required for the target lift. There was a single analysis at the planned end date, with no early looks. Treatment leads in the pooled total and within each platform, with the same traffic mix in both arms. The primary metric was completed signups per visitor, and treatment showed a 7.4% relative lift over control. The lift is stable across all four weeks with no fade after the first days. Based on this, we recommend rolling the treatment out to everyone.

We recommend rolling the simplified form out to everyone.

Recommendation: roll the personalized shelf out to all users.

Control got 50,200 visitors and treatment 50,100 under a planned even split. The change was a new “For You” recommendation shelf on the podcast home feed, replacing the static “Trending” row. The team recommends rolling the shelf out to all users.
